question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat unknown children of the runtime-owned `meta` object as accepted and preserved forward-compatible bookkeeping, while keeping every operational configuration namespace strict?
rationale: This is not a mechanical repair choice: it establishes a public configuration compatibility boundary that affects future writers and version interoperability.

options.title: Accept the narrow metadata contract
options.body: Merge after final-head runtime proof, documenting that only `meta` may contain unknown bookkeeping fields and that operational configuration remains fail-closed.

options.title: Keep `meta` strict
options.body: Close or revise the PR and require known metadata additions to arrive through explicit schema and migration changes.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow metadata contract
recommendation.body: Merge after final-head runtime proof, documenting that only `meta` may contain unknown bookkeeping fields and that operational configuration remains fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The final-head update directly reconciled this change with the current schema architecture and generated config contract.
